Hi Alex 

Great to meet you today appreciate the detailed questions. Quick recap + proposed next steps below, and I’ve looped in Rishi (security) and Neha (solutions) so they can join the technical review.

Recap / answers (high level):
- Default hosted behavior: We capture request metadata (timestamps, route, model, latency, token counts) and request/response payloads only if customers opt into "full logging" for debugging. By default, request/response bodies are NOT retained for production workloads unless enabled.
- Headers: We redact standard sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie) by default in logs. Custom header redaction can be configured via a redaction ruleset (header name patterns).
- PII redaction/masking: We support configurable redaction pipelines: regex-based masking (credit card, SSN), token-based detection (NER + patterns), and policy rules to replace detected PII with deterministic pseudonyms (e.g., <REDACTED_EMAIL_123>). We also support user-supplied allowlists/denylists.
- Zero-logging mode: Yes for Dedicated and Private deployments we offer a zero-logging option (no request/response bodies, only minimal access/audit records). For hosted customers, a per-route logging toggle and per-customer policy can be enforced to prevent storing bodies.
- Retention: Default retention for request metadata/access logs is 90 days for hosted plans but can be shortened to 30/14/0 days via config. Payload retention (if enabled) is configurable; recommended pattern is 7–30 days depending on debug needs. For Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed retention policies and on-prem log archiving.
- Trace IDs: Trace IDs are stored as hashed values in logs by default (SHA-256 salt per customer) to allow cross-request correlation without exposing raw IDs. We can provide an HMAC option for reversible mapping under customer KMS control if you need to map traces back during incident response.

Attachments: I’m attaching a short redaction design draft and our SOC 2 summary to start (redaction_design_draft.pdf, SOC2-summary-2026.pdf).

3) We'll ship a short PoC config (redaction rules + retention policy) you can test against a staging route.

Thanks that all sounds promising. Two quick clarifying questions before the call: 
1) For credit card PANs and government tax IDs that sometimes appear in free text, do you support deterministic tokenization (so the same PAN maps to the same token) or do you only support irreversible redaction?
2) If we enable "no payload retention" for a route, do request IDs/trace IDs still get emitted to logs (hashed) so we can trace errors?

If you can give short answers here we can be prepared on our side.

—Alex

Subject: Re: Logging & redaction controls quick clarifying Qs

Alex 

Short answers:
- Deterministic tokenization: Supported. We offer deterministic pseudonymization for identifiers where you want consistent mapping (e.g., tokenized PANs) using customer-scoped salts/HSM keys. That lets you correlate across requests without storing the raw value.
- No payload retention + traceability: Yes if you enable no-payload retention, we still emit minimal request metadata and hashed trace IDs so you can correlate events. Payloads/bodies are not stored. Trace IDs are hashed by default; reversible HMAC mapping is optional under KMS control.
